headline: Morocco defeats Netherlands in tie-breaker to advance to FIFA World Cup Round of 16
summary: Morocco secured their spot in the FIFA World Cup Round of 16 after a thrilling penalty shootout victory over the Netherlands. The match ended 1-1 after extra time before the African team triumphed 3-2 in the tie-breaker.
details: Morocco has advanced to the FIFA World Cup Round of 16 after defeating the Netherlands in a dramatic penalty shootout in their Round of 32 match. The game was a nail-biter from start to finish.
The two teams were locked in a 1-1 draw at the end of regular time, pushing the match into an additional 30 minutes of extra time. Both sides fought hard for a decisive goal.
However, neither team could break the deadlock during the extended period, leading to a tense tie-breaker to determine the winner. The pressure was immense on both goalkeepers and penalty takers.

In the penalty shootout, Morocco emerged victorious with a 3-2 scoreline, securing their much-coveted ticket to the next stage of the tournament. This win marks a significant achievement for the African squad.

headline: Bangladesh Bank to announce new monetary policy today
summary: The central bank will outline its plan for the first half of the new fiscal year, focusing on inflation control and economic growth.
details: Bangladesh Bank is set to announce its monetary policy for the first half of the new fiscal year this Tuesday afternoon, June 30.
The policy will detail the plan for the amount of money supply in the market to implement the government's financial goals.
Key priorities for the upcoming policy include controlling high inflation, boosting private sector credit growth, and maintaining economic momentum.
The new guidelines will be effective from July to December of this year, following the central bank's practice of updating policy every six months.
Previously, on February 9, the policy interest rate was kept unchanged at 10% to combat inflation, as announced by former Governor Ahsan H. Mansur.
Since late 2022, Bangladesh Bank has consistently raised interest rates to curb rising prices across the country.
Following the formation of the BNP government in February, initiatives have been taken to increase credit flow to the private sector.
The latest national budget also includes a special loan package of 60,000 crore BDT to help restart closed factories.
caption:
How will the central bank tackle inflation and boost growth? Bangladesh Bank announces its new monetary policy today.

Bangladesh Bank is set to announce its monetary policy for the first half of the new fiscal year this Tuesday afternoon, June 30.

The policy will detail the plan for the amount of money supply in the market to implement the government's financial goals.

Key priorities for the upcoming policy include controlling high inflation, boosting private sector credit growth, and maintaining economic momentum.

The new guidelines will be effective from July to December of this year, following the central bank's practice of updating policy every six months.

Previously, on February 9, the policy interest rate was kept unchanged at 10% to combat inflation, as announced by former Governor Ahsan H. Mansur.

Since late 2022, Bangladesh Bank has consistently raised interest rates to curb rising prices across the country.

Following the formation of the BNP government in February, initiatives have been taken to increase credit flow to the private sector.

The latest national budget also includes a special loan package of 60,000 crore BDT to help restart closed factories.
